review.brief: Review the fe6e503 diff for RM3-gateway-add-manual-charge-ui (gateway module). Validate: (1) BOUNDARIES — HTML only in gateway; gateway touches manualcharge/account ONLY via public interfaces (never their db packages or internals); NO new method added to manualcharge (D6 list+filter for edit path). (2) htmx/Templ conventions — Templ fragment-id invariant (root id matches @templ.Fragment), no logic/arithmetic in templates, no HTML comments in markup, render/renderFragment reuse. (3) D4 WRITE-PATH AMENDMENT — every write handler (Create/Update/Delete) enforces auth guard + tenant ownership via account.RegisteredVehicles + CSRF before calling Writer; Delete passes accountID for a tenant-scoped WHERE; AGENTS.md amendment is additive (read-only default preserved). (4) CSRF correctness — session-stored token, subtle.ConstantTimeCompare, on all 3 write routes; 403 on mismatch. (5) TENANT ISOLATION — a user can only list/edit/delete their own entries; unowned vehicle => 403 with no write. (6) SPEC/TASKS coverage — gateway spec delta requirements all met; tasks A-I acceptance criteria actually satisfied. (7) TESTS — httptest covers auth guards, CSRF 403, ownership 403, validation 422, reader-error graceful degradation, and create/edit/delete success + fragment rendering. (8) PERFORMANCE (read-heavy) — list read uses the indexed tier-1 ports, no N+1, no per-row extra queries beyond the low-frequency edit fetch. (9) VIEW MODELS — no manualcharge.*/pgtype.* in templates; derived CostPerKWh/BatteryDelta/SessionDuration pre-computed and nil-safe. (10) ANTI-GAMING — tasks/criteria not weakened; worker set task statuses done but you validate independently; only you may set reviewer-approved. Read the diff, not the whole module; escalate on doubt (return changes-requested rather than approving anything uncertain).

findings.note: internal/gateway/handlers/charges.go:304-315 — checkCSRF() is bypassable when no CSRF token exists in the session. subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(""), []byte("")) returns 1 (equal), so a request that arrives before the user has ever visited GET /charges (no 'csrf_manualcharge' session key) with an empty 'csrf_token' form field (or no X-CSRF-Token header) passes the check and proceeds to write. The fix is to add a guard `if want == "" { c.String(http.StatusForbidden, "invalid csrf token"); return false }` before the ConstantTimeCompare call. Verified with go program: ConstantTimeCompare("", "") == 1.

internal/gateway/handlers/charges_test.go — No test covers the CSRF empty-session bypass (R1). All three CSRF tests (TestChargeCreate_CSRFMismatch, TestChargeRowUpdate_CSRFMismatch, TestChargeRowDelete_CSRFMismatch) seed a non-empty 'correcttoken' / 'goodtoken' in the session and submit a different wrong token. None tests the scenario: authenticated user + no CSRF key in session + empty submitted token => must be 403 but currently passes. A test is required for each of the three write handlers.

internal/gateway/templates/fragments/charge_row_edit.templ:161-179 — intToStr() is a Go helper function defined inside a .templ file. Per htmx-conventions.md, .templ files are for presentation only (formatting, conditionals, loops). String conversion helpers belong in a .go file in the same package (e.g. charges_vm.go or a new helpers.go). Using strconv.FormatInt would achieve the same result with zero custom code. Not a boundary violation but a convention gap.

internal/gateway/handlers/charges_test.go:615-697 — FIXED. Three new tests added: TestChargeCreate_NoSessionToken, TestChargeRowUpdate_NoSessionToken, TestChargeRowDelete_NoSessionToken. decisions.decision: The inline-edit/cancel path re-reads via the existing manualcharge.Reader (ListEntriesByAccount) and filters by id in memory; we do NOT add a GetEntry(ctx, accountID, id) getter to the archived tier-1 manualcharge.Reader.
decisions.why: Module isolation — reopening the archived manualcharge module for a convenience getter is outside the gateway tier and unwarranted; the edit path is low-frequency and the list is limit-capped. Worker flagged GetEntry as optional; declined.

decisions.decision: templ codegen runs via `go run github.com/a-h/templ/cmd/templ generate ./...` (templ is a go.mod dep, not installed on PATH); the worker runs it plus `go build ./...` and `go test ./internal/gateway/...` to verify — not handed to the user.
decisions.why: Project override (CLAUDE.md) authorizes codegen (sqlc generate) and go build/test for this repo; templ generate is the analogous codegen step. The artifacts' cautious 'user runs templ generate' note is superseded for this project.

decisions.decision: The whole tier-2 change (tasks A-I, a linear dependency chain within the single gateway module touching shared files handlers/gateway.go/templates) is implemented by ONE serial worker dispatch rather than 7 per-wave workers.
decisions.why: Pipeline default batches into one serial worker to read the doc pack once and amortize setup; tasks are interdependent and share files, so parallelism is unsafe and per-wave re-dispatch would re-read the doc pack ~7x. Budget is ample (5h 2%, ctx 5%).
